caution: A failure to reproduce is not a finding that the paper is wrong. It may be a failure of the attempt.

attempts.label: CRCNS:aa-3
attempts.entry_title: Uva lesions and multiunit activity in Uva during singing (Danish, Aronov and Fee 2017)
attempts.summary: In this data the paper's main findings on zebra finch Uva activity during song largely hold up: multiunit activity rises during singing, dips before syllable offsets and leads song amplitude, though each bird's Uva channel had to be guessed. After Uva lesions, song lost structure as reported in all 7 birds, mostly with values that differ from the paper's, and the drop in maturity index appears only under a spectral measure the agent assumed. Lesioned birds sang less per hour, where the paper reports similar rates, but only under one way of counting song. The loss of directed song and the control lesions could not be tested, as the dataset lacks directed-song labels and control birds.
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Danish, Aronov and Fee (2017) on CRCNS aa-3, which holds song from 7 zebra finches before and after bilateral Uva lesions, with the authors' segmentations, and multiunit recordings in Uva during singing from 3 of the paper's 5 recorded birds. It tests the lesion effects on song structure and rhythm, and the timing, consistency and rhythm of Uva activity relative to syllables, song amplitude and spectral song features. Control lesions, marked directed song, sorted single units and GTE times are not in the data set.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Danish et al. (2017) from CRCNS aa-3

outcomes.statement: After complete bilateral Uva lesions, birds presented with a female court her but do not sing; they produce only sporadic short sounds like introductory notes without their rhythm.
outcomes.source: Results, Uva is necessary for adult stereotyped song, paragraph 1; S1 Video
outcomes.quote: However, consistent with previous reports [ 26 , 27 ], lesioned birds failed to sing and only produced sporadic short sounds, acoustically similar to introductory notes but without their characteristic rhythmicity
outcomes.notes: The lesion folders hold one day before and one day after the lesion per bird. The paper and the data descriptor say directed song was recorded, but neither the wav file names (bird, date number, date and time), their analysis files (which carry no properties) nor the descriptor mark any recording as directed, so directed recordings, if present, cannot be told apart.

outcomes.statement: In social isolation, Uva-lesioned birds sing at rates similar to intact birds.
outcomes.source: Results, Uva is necessary for adult stereotyped song, paragraph 2
outcomes.quote: While Uva lesions completely abolished directed singing, lesioned birds in social isolation sang at rates similar as intact birds in social isolation
outcomes.notes: Per hour of the recording span (first to last file of the day), selected syllables per hour fall after the lesion in 6 of 7 birds (post/pre ratios 0.08 to 1.01, Wilcoxon p = 0.031); bouts per hour p = 0.047, singing time per hour p = 0.031. The result rests on counting the selected segments; with all segments, selected or not, the decreases are not significant (segments, bouts and singing time per hour p = 0.078, 0.109 and 0.078), and the selected fraction differs between days (Purple53 0.59 before, 0.34 after). Per hour of recorded audio, all segments give p = 1.000 and selected segments p = 0.078, but recordings are triggered by sound. Spans range from 2.2 to 41.6 h, so the span is a weak measure of time; raw bout counts per day do not differ significantly (p = 0.156) but are not a rate. Only one day per condition is in the data set, so the two readings of the days compared coincide.
deviations: The recording hours are taken as the span between the first and last file of the day, as the files hold no record of when the recorder was running (an assumption).

Song is counted from the segments the authors selected in their analysis files, assumed to be the song syllables they analysed; all segments are shown as a variant and do not give a significant decrease.

outcomes.statement: Uva lesions lower the maturity index, a measure of song repeatability, from 0.26 to 0.08 (Wilcoxon signed-rank test, p < 0.025, 7 birds).
outcomes.source: Results, Uva is necessary for adult stereotyped song, paragraph 2; Fig 2G
outcomes.quote: Uva lesions cause a significant decrease in a measure of song repeatability (maturity index; M pre = 0.26±0.03, M post = 0.08±0.02; p<0.025, Wilcoxon signed rank test, n = 7 lesioned birds, ±SD
outcomes.notes: With log spectra centred and scaled per frequency on the condition's mean spectrum, lag reading (a) and 300 ms bout gaps, MI is 0.235 +- 0.087 before and 0.096 +- 0.031 after, both within tolerance, falling in all 7 birds (Wilcoxon p = 0.016). This is the only one of the 16 combinations of form, lag reading and gap that puts both values in tolerance, and the form is this attempt's, not a reading the claims file lists, so the outcome is partial. With 350 ms gaps, 0.213 and 0.098 (pre just outside). Lag reading (b) gives 0.355 and 0.249 (decrease in 7 of 7, values outside). Read literally (Pearson correlation of raw power or log power spectra), MI does not fall (0 to 2 birds decrease) and lies between 0.32 and 0.62, far from the paper's values; the shared background spectrum makes silent slices correlate. Only one post-lesion day is in the data set, so the claims file's two readings of the post-lesion day coincide.
deviations: Assumed that the power spectra are log-scaled and that each frequency's mean (over all slices of the bird's condition) is removed, and divided by its SD, before correlating. The Methods say only "correlation of power spectra" and cite Aronov et al. 2008, which this run could not read. The literal reading cannot give values near the paper's 0.08, so it is unlikely to be the paper's computation; all four forms are shown. Asked of the authors (methods_unavailable).
100 bouts per bird and condition drawn with a fixed seed from bouts of 0.7 to 2 s built from the selected segments of the authors' analysis files.

outcomes.statement: After Uva lesions syllable-duration distributions are much closer to exponential (goodness of fit Gamma 3.7 against 16 before; Wilcoxon signed-rank test, p < 0.025, 7 birds), but stay above the subsong criterion of Gamma < 2.
outcomes.source: Results, Uva is necessary for adult stereotyped song, paragraph 3; Fig 2C and 2F
outcomes.quote: Post-lesion syllable duration distributions are significantly closer to exponential (Γ post = 3.7±1.2) than are pre-lesion songs (Γ pre = 16±6) (p<0.025, Wilcoxon signed rank test, n = 7 lesioned birds) ( Fig 2F ), but do not meet the strictest criterion for subsong (Γ < 2)
outcomes.notes: Durations of the selected segments of each day (2,129 to 20,127 syllables). Reading (a), D times root n, gives 30.41 +- 6.31 before and 15.19 +- 6.57 after; reading (b), D over the Lilliefors critical value, 28.69 and 14.33. Both fall in all 7 birds (Wilcoxon p = 0.0156) and stay above 2, but are about twice the paper's 16 and 3.7. The raw D falls from 0.29 to 0.21. The one SyllGaps.mat file (Purple94 post-lesion) gives Gamma 9.26, lower than the analysis file's 16.32 for the same day, so the authors' segmentation for Gamma may differ from the analysis files.
deviations: The scale of Gamma is not defined in the paper; ref 41 could not be read in this run, so the claims file's two readings were used.

outcomes.statement: In 6 of 7 Uva-lesioned birds the post-lesion syllable-duration distribution has a small peak at 50 to 100 ms.
outcomes.source: Results, Uva is necessary for adult stereotyped song, paragraph 3; Fig 2C
outcomes.quote: Indeed, in the majority of Uva-lesioned birds (n = 6/7), a small peak is seen in the syllable distribution at 50-100ms
outcomes.notes: With 5 ms bins all 7 lesioned birds have a local maximum between 50 and 100 ms above the fitted exponential, and above its 97.5% Poisson bound (readings a and b). With 10 ms bins (variant) 6 of 7 do (Red92 has none), the paper's count. The main count is 7 against 6.

outcomes.statement: After Uva lesions gap durations become broadly distributed, with more long and more short gaps, like subsong.
outcomes.source: Results, Uva is necessary for adult stereotyped song, paragraph 4; Fig 2D
outcomes.quote: Following Uva lesions, however, gap durations become more broadly distributed, with an increased incidence of long and short gaps
outcomes.notes: Reading (a), 16 to 38% of post-lesion gaps fall outside the bird's pre-lesion 5th to 95th percentiles (10% if unchanged; Wilcoxon p = 0.016); the long fraction exceeds 5% in all 7 birds (11 to 26%) and the short fraction in 6 of 7 (Purple53 2.9%). Reading (b), the interquartile range of log gap widens in 5 of 7 birds (p = 0.078).

outcomes.statement: Uva lesions decrease song rhythmicity, R, from 3.30 to 1.7 (Wilcoxon signed-rank test, p < 0.025, 7 birds).
outcomes.source: Results, Uva is necessary for adult stereotyped song, paragraph 5; Fig 2E
outcomes.quote: the increase in variability in both syllable and gap durations following Uva lesions is accompanied by a significant decrease in rhythmicity of song temporal structure in post-lesion birds ( Fig 2E ; R pre = 3.30±1.1, R post = 1.7±0.3; p<0.025 Wilcoxon signed rank test, n = 7 lesioned birds
outcomes.notes: With the dB amplitude and null (a), R is 4.84 +- 1.69 before and 2.44 +- 0.45 after, falling in all 7 birds (Wilcoxon p = 0.016); null (b) gives 5.87 and 2.41 (p = 0.016). Both values are above the paper's tolerances. The log of the rectified amplitude (reading c) gives ratios dominated by 25 to 30 Hz and no consistent decrease (2 of 7 birds).
deviations: Bouts shorter than 1 s, and longer than 4.1 s, are left out (the shortest is not given; a standard choice for a 4 Hz taper resolution). R is the maximum between 3 and 30 Hz (the upper bound is not given; 3 to 50 Hz is shown).
The synthetic null uses square syllable and gap levels at the bird's mean levels, smoothed at 2.5 ms, averaged over 5 synthetic bout sets; the paper does not describe the synthetic amplitude.

outcomes.statement: Unlike subsong, 6 of 7 Uva-lesioned birds keep a significant peak in the song rhythm spectrum between 3 and 8 Hz.
outcomes.source: Results, Uva is necessary for adult stereotyped song, paragraph 5; Fig 2E legend
outcomes.quote: However, unlike subsong birds that had no significant rhythmicity, 6 of 7 Uva-lesioned birds exhibited a significant peak in the power spectrum between 3-8Hz
outcomes.notes: With 1000 synthetic null sets per bird, all 7 lesioned birds have a ratio maximum between 3 and 8 Hz (2.11 to 3.34) above the 95th percentile of the same maximum over the null sets (1.11 to 1.26), and all 7 between 4 and 8 Hz. The paper reports 6 of 7 with tolerance 0. In 3 birds (Purple94, LPink13, LPink15) the 3 to 8 Hz maximum is the band's lower edge, 3.17 Hz. Requiring a local maximum inside the band, all 7 still pass (local maxima 1.286 to 3.342, at 5.1 to 7.1 Hz, against null thresholds of 1.11 to 1.26), as the synthetic null has no amplitude texture within syllables. Requiring the peak's prominence to exceed the 95th percentile of the null's prominences, 4 of 7 pass in 3 to 8 Hz and 5 of 7 in 4 to 8 Hz. No version gives 6 of 7. For post-lesion song the two null readings are the same.
deviations: The local-maximum and prominence tests are added variants; the claims file's test takes the ratio's maximum in the band.

outcomes.statement: Control lesions 250 um dorsal or 200 um ventral to Uva have no significant effect on syllable or gap duration distributions, maturity index or song rhythm (p > 0.50, 4 birds).
outcomes.source: Results, Uva is necessary for adult stereotyped song, paragraph 6; S1 Fig
outcomes.quote: these control lesions had no effect on song structure as assessed in song spectrograms, nor did they have a significant effect on syllable or gap duration distributions (p>0.50 for all measurements, n = 4 birds), on maturity index (p>0.50), or song rhythm spectrum (p>0.50)
outcomes.notes: The lesion archive holds 7 birds, all with pre- and post-lesion folders, matching the paper's 7 Uva-lesioned birds; the 4 control-lesion birds are not in it.

outcomes.statement: Antidromic responses of Uva neurons to HVC stimulation have short latencies (1.5 to 5 ms) and small jitter (< 100 us), and can be elicited by stimulation intensities of 70 to 300 uA.
outcomes.source: Results, Song-related activity in Uva, paragraph 1; Fig 3B and 3C
outcomes.quote: Antidromic responses had short latencies (1.5-5ms) with a small jitter (<100μs), and could be elicited by stimulation intensity of 70–300μA
outcomes.notes: The claims file makes the claim untestable without stimulation recordings with stimulus times, and its latency and jitter are those of identified single units. The archive holds the stimulation files (the spreadsheets mark them "stim", at 150, 200 and 320 uA; 40 of them have artefacts on the chosen channel), but no stimulus times and no sorted or identified units. The notebook describes the artefacts; they come back to within 0.25 V of baseline a median 2.3 ms after onset (1.3 to 8.7 ms over files), inside the 1.5 to 5 ms window, and 36 of 779 stimuli have recovered before 1.5 ms. In a multiunit trace a response locked to the stimulus with under 100 us of jitter repeats on every trial like the artefact and cannot be told apart from it without identified units and collision tests, so no antidromic response was looked for and none is reported either way. The 320 uA of Orange150 lies inside the claim's widened 63 to 330 uA range.

outcomes.statement: HVC-projecting Uva neurons recorded off song fire regularly at 20 to 50 Hz (4 neurons, 2 birds), while units just dorsal or ventral to the core appear to fire much less, below 10 Hz (5 neurons).
outcomes.source: Results, Song-related activity in Uva, paragraph 1
outcomes.quote: Single-unit recordings of HVC-projecting Uva neurons during non-singing revealed regular spontaneous spiking at 20-50Hz (n = 4 neurons, n = 2 birds). Single-units recorded just dorsal or ventral to HVC-projecting core of Uva appeared to exhibit much lower rates of spontaneous spiking (n = 5 neurons, <10Hz)
outcomes.notes: The analysis files hold no spike times (EventTimes empty in all five) and no sorted units; the 32 "spontaneous activity" recordings are raw multiunit signals with no unit identities and nothing to say which units project to HVC.

outcomes.statement: Uva activity rises sharply just before distance calls, leaving baseline 30 ms and peaking 15 ms before call onset.
outcomes.source: Results, Song-related activity in Uva, paragraph 2; Fig 4C
outcomes.quote: Uva activity increases sharply immediately prior to the onset of distance calls ( Fig 4C ; latency from baseline = 30±7ms, latency from peak = 15±5ms, ±SD)
outcomes.notes: Calls are the segments labelled "k" (145 in b871, 86 in Uva4; Orange150 has none labelled). The call-aligned MUA peaks 13 and 17 ms before onset (mean 15.0; paper 15 +- 5). Only Uva4 rises above the inside-bout band, 22 ms before onset (paper 30 +- 7); b871 does not, and against a band drawn from the call files neither does. The measured latency from baseline is Uva4's alone.
deviations: The label "k" is read as distance calls from its duration (about 210 ms) and from the spreadsheets, which mark the files where it occurs as distance calls; the data set does not name its labels.
Rests on the channel chosen for each bird (see fig4a-elevated-during-song).

outcomes.statement: Uva is robustly active before each introductory note, leaving baseline 39 ms and peaking 21 ms before note onset.
outcomes.source: Results, Song-related activity in Uva, paragraph 2; Fig 4B
outcomes.quote: One of the most prominent features of Uva activity during singing is the robust activation prior to each introductory note ( Fig 4B , latency from baseline = 39±8ms, peak latency = 21±9ms, ±SD)
outcomes.notes: Introductory notes are the segments labelled "i" (20 in b871, 113 in Orange150, 10 in Uva4). The average peaks 20, 24 and 26 ms before onset (mean 23.3; paper 21 +- 9). Under shuffle reading (b), with the windows cut from the shifted bout taken as periodic, Orange150 and Uva4 leave the band 36 and 38 ms before onset (mean 37.0 over these two birds; paper 39 +- 8); b871 does not. Under reading (a) the band for maxima, built from as few as 10 windows, is wide and no bird leaves it.
deviations: Rests on the channel chosen for each bird.

outcomes.statement: During bouts of singing Uva activity is persistently elevated and modulated in a way locked to song.
outcomes.source: Results, Song-related activity in Uva, paragraph 2; Fig 4A
outcomes.quote: During bouts of singing, Uva activity is persistently elevated and is strongly modulated in a manner locked to song
outcomes.notes: On the chosen channels mean MUA inside bouts exceeds MUA more than 300 ms from any segment at all 18 sites (ratios 1.04 to 2.13; paired t-test over sites t = 7.09, p = 1.8e-06). The other channels are higher inside bouts at 3 to 7 of 4 to 7 sites, with median ratios 1.01 to 1.19.
deviations: Assumed that the neural channel of each bird is the one of its three with the largest range of the syllable-onset-aligned MUA (b871 channel 6, Orange150 channel 7, Uva4 channel 3). The paper describes one electrode and the data set does not say which channel it is; channels 5 and 6 of Orange150 are near copies of each other. The choice uses the syllable modulation that later claims measure, so it favours finding modulation, though not its timing. Asked of the authors.
Files whose properties mark them above, below or outside Uva are left out.

outcomes.statement: Uva activity is consistent across renditions of the song motif; time-warped MUA is correlated across renditions (0.64 with 5 ms smoothing) and coherent below 12 Hz (mean coherence 0.68 between 1 and 12 Hz).
outcomes.source: Results, Song-related activity in Uva, paragraph 2; Fig 5A to 5C
outcomes.quote: the smoothed multiunit signals are highly correlated across different song renditions (0.64±0.06 with 5ms smoothing) and coherent across different song renditions at frequencies below 12Hz (C avg = 0.68±0.09 between 1-12Hz, ±SD)
outcomes.notes: 112, 153 and 44 motif renditions. Reading (a), all pairs, gives correlation 0.701 (paper 0.64 +- 0.06, just above) and coherence 0.585 over 1 to 12 Hz (paper 0.68 +- 0.09, just below); reading (b) correlation 0.740; reading (c), against the mean of the others, 0.829 and 0.730. All are far above the shifted null (95th percentile of the 1 to 12 Hz maximum 0.21 to 0.35). No reading puts both in tolerance.
deviations: The motif of each bird is its most common sequence of motif letters (abcd, abcdefgh, abcdef), taken from the labels.
Coherence over all pairs uses a random sample of 2000 pairs where there are more.

outcomes.statement: Uva activity is similar at different recording depths along a penetration; correlation 0.62 with 5 ms smoothing and mean coherence 0.65 between 1 and 12 Hz, with no evidence that activity varies across sites.
outcomes.source: Results, Song-related activity in Uva, paragraph 3; Fig 5D to 5F
outcomes.quote: We find that activity at different recording sites throughout Uva is also highly correlated (0.62±0.03 with 5ms smoothing) and coherent (C avg = 0.65±0.13 between 1-12Hz, ±SD)
outcomes.notes: Sites with at least 5 renditions, paired within a recording day (3 pairs in b871, 3 in Orange150, 6 in Uva4). Coherence between single renditions of two sites averages 0.688 (paper 0.65 +- 0.13). Correlation is higher than the paper's, 0.893 between site averages (reading a) and 0.705 between single renditions (reading b; paper 0.62 +- 0.03).
deviations: Coherence of two site averages with one taper is identically 1, so coherence is taken from single renditions (reading b) under both readings.
The penetration of each Uva4 site is not recorded (its spreadsheet lists three dates, its analysis file one folder); all Uva4 sites are paired.

outcomes.statement: Uva activity rises significantly before syllable onsets in every bird, peaking 20 ms before onset and rising above its average level during singing 32 ms before onset.
outcomes.source: Results, Song-related activity in Uva, paragraph 4; Fig 6A, 6B and 6D; S2 and S3 Figs
outcomes.quote: exhibiting a significant increase in activity prior to syllable onsets (p<0.01 paired t-test) ... significant for each bird recorded; n = 5). Uva activity peaks 20±2ms (±SEM) prior to syllable onsets, and rises significantly above the average level of activity during singing 32±5ms before syllable onsets
outcomes.notes: The onset-aligned MUA peaks 13, 16 and 22 ms before onset (mean 17.0, SEM 2.6; paper 20 +- 2, outside) and rises above the band 25, 27 and 32 ms before (mean 28.0 under shuffle a, 29.0 under b; paper 32 +- 5, within). The 40 ms before onset exceed the bout mean and the window at the preceding offset in every bird (paired t-tests, p below 1e-24). The peak time depends on the assumed channel; b871's channel 7 peaks 18 ms before onset against 13 ms on channel 6, which would make the mean 18.7 ms, within the tolerance, though on channel 7 the b871 average does not rise above the band before onset.
deviations: Rests on the channel chosen for each bird (see fig4a-elevated-during-song).

outcomes.statement: Uva activity falls significantly before syllable offsets in every bird, reaching a minimum 18 ms before offset and dropping below its average level during singing 48 ms before offset.
outcomes.source: Results, Song-related activity in Uva, paragraph 4; Fig 6C and 6E; S2 and S3 Figs
outcomes.quote: a significant decrease prior to syllable offsets ( Fig 6B ; significant for each bird recorded; n = 5) ... The decrease in Uva activity at syllable offsets reaches a minimum 18±1ms (±SEM) prior to the offset ( Fig 6D ) and drops significantly below average Uva activity during singing 48±8ms prior to the offset
outcomes.notes: The minimum averages 18.0 ms before offset (12, 17 and 25 ms; paper 18 +- 1) and the average drops below the band 40.7 ms before offset under shuffle reading (b) (40, 43 and 39 ms; paper 48 +- 8; 36.3 under reading a, outside). The 50 ms before offset are below the bout mean and the 40 ms before the next onset in every bird (p below 1e-7). The drop time sits 0.7 ms inside the tolerance.
deviations: Rests on the channel chosen for each bird (see fig4a-elevated-during-song).

outcomes.statement: Uva activity correlates with song amplitude (peak correlation 0.40) and leads it by 42 ms.
outcomes.source: Results, Song-related activity in Uva, paragraph 4; Fig 7A
outcomes.quote: Uva activity is also strongly correlated with song amplitude (magnitude of peak correlation ... 0.40±0.04), with a latency of 42±6ms ( Fig 7A , ± S.D)
outcomes.notes: With motif segments and the rectified amplitude (reading c), peak correlation 0.382 with MUA leading by 40.7 ms (paper 0.40 +- 0.04 at 42 +- 6). Bouts with the same amplitude give 0.459 at 40.7 ms (just outside); the dB amplitude gives 0.55 to 0.60 at 26 to 38 ms; power without the log 0.32 to 0.35.
deviations: Bouts of 1 to 8.192 s (3 longer Uva4 bouts left out).

outcomes.statement: None of six spectral song features correlates significantly with Uva activity within a bird; pooled over birds only amplitude (r = 0.18) and gravity center (r = 0.17) do, after Bonferroni correction.
outcomes.source: Results, Song-related activity in Uva, paragraph 5
outcomes.quote: None of these six spectral features is significantly correlated with Uva activity in individual birds. When combined across all birds, only amplitude (r = 0.18) and gravity center (r = 0.17) exhibit significant correlation after Bonferroni correction for multiple comparisons (6 comparisons; p<0.008)

statistics.about: amplitude and gravity center, all birds combined

outcomes.notes: Six features computed per 1 ms from the raw audio by uva.sap_features. Within single birds, 9 of 18 bird-feature pairs correlate significantly with MUA (Bonferroni over 6 features) per rendition (reading a) and 15 of 18 per 1 ms bin (reading b); the paper reports none. Amplitude alone breaks the single-bird condition (reading a, b871 p = 0.0074 and Uva4 p = 0.0012; reading b, all three birds). Pooled over birds, amplitude r = 0.156 (a) and 0.183 (b, within 0.18 +- 0.018); gravity center r = 0.291 (a) and 0.082 (b), outside 0.17 +- 0.017; pitch goodness and FM are significant under every pooling, and Wiener entropy under (a) and (b) but not with features z-scored within syllable type (p = 0.06). The single-bird tests use 317 to 2138 renditions and 31k to 257k bins per bird, so correlations as small as 0.058 are significant; the paper does not give its n.
deviations: The features follow Sound Analysis Pro's definitions only approximately (a Hann taper where SAP uses two Slepian tapers, and the helper's own forms of FM and pitch goodness), as the claims file adopts SAP's definitions as an assumption.

outcomes.statement: Song amplitude and Uva activity both have a broad spectral peak near 10 Hz, at 8.0 Hz for song and 8.8 Hz for Uva.
outcomes.source: Results, Song-related activity in Uva, paragraph 6; Fig 7B
outcomes.quote: we found that the song amplitude profile of our adult birds exhibits a broad spectral peak near this frequency ( Fig 7B ; peak of average song rhythm spectrum at 8.0Hz). Notably, Uva multiunit activity also exhibits peaks at nearly the same frequency (8.8Hz)
outcomes.notes: With each spectrum normalized by its sum, over motifs with the dB amplitude, the average spectra peak at 9.03 Hz for song and 8.91 Hz for MUA (paper 8.0 and 8.8); MUA is within tolerance, song just above it (7.2 to 8.8). The power and rectified amplitudes give 9.28 Hz. Normalized by length and averaged without renormalizing, the MUA peak moves to 12.6 Hz over motifs and 11.6 Hz over bouts. Over bouts the song amplitude peaks at 6.10 to 6.23 Hz. No reading puts both peaks in tolerance.
deviations: Rests on the channel chosen for each bird (see fig4a-elevated-during-song).

outcomes.statement: Uva activity and song amplitude are significantly coherent near 10 Hz (peak at 8.8 Hz, coherence 0.75, p < 0.01, phase -0.77 pi), with a large peak in their cross-spectrum.
outcomes.source: Results, Song-related activity in Uva, paragraph 6; Fig 7C and 7D
outcomes.quote: Further analysis reveals a large peak in the cross spectral density between multiunit activity and song amplitude, as well as a significant coherency at this frequency (F peak = 8.8Hz, C peak = 0.75, p<0.01, phase = -0.77π)

statistics.test: coherency against a null of randomly shifted MUA, corrected for multiple testing

outcomes.notes: Over motifs with the amplitude as power (reading b), the bird-averaged coherency peaks at 9.03 Hz, coherence 0.789, phase -0.721 pi as Chronux returns it for (MUA, amplitude), above the null of shifted MUA (99th percentile of maxima 0.209, p = 0.001 with 1000 shifts). The dB and rectified amplitudes peak at 8.79 and 8.91 Hz with coherence 0.85 (outside) and phase -0.80 and -0.74 pi. Over bouts the peak is at 6.3 Hz.
deviations: Coherency is averaged over segments within a bird (Chronux trial averaging), then over birds.

outcomes.statement: Uva activity shows no significant correlation with gesture trajectory extrema (GTEs), in single birds or averaged across birds, against GTE times shuffled within syllables.
outcomes.source: Results, Song-related activity in Uva, paragraph 7; Fig 8D to 8F
outcomes.quote: No significant peaks are observed in this correlation within individual birds or averaged across birds, compared to surrogate datasets in which GTE times are randomly shuffled within song syllables
outcomes.notes: Not attempted. GTE times need the syrinx-model method of Boari et al. (ref 50). The paper links no code; a third-party copy of GTE extraction code from the Mindlin lab exists (github.com/kylerbrown/mindlin_auto), which is not the paper's implementation and was not tried in this run.

outcomes.statement: In long syllables (> 150 ms; 13 syllables, 43% of song syllables) Uva activity can oscillate fast; 8 of 13 have a significant spectral peak above 10 Hz, at 17 to 51 Hz, and Uva activity is coherent with song amplitude from 1 to 55 Hz.
outcomes.source: Results, Song-related activity in Uva, paragraph 8; Fig 9A to 9D; S4 Fig
outcomes.quote: analysis done for 13 syllables longer than 150ms, in order to provide adequate sample duration; this was 43% of all song syllables). Of these 13 syllables, 8 syllables show a significant peak in the spectrum of the neural activity greater than 10Hz. These peaks occur at frequencies ranging from 17 to 51Hz. Notably, in individual syllables, Uva activity and sound amplitude are found to be significantly coherent across a broad range of frequencies (1-55Hz)
outcomes.notes: 6 of 18 syllable types (3 birds) have a median duration above 150 ms (0.33; paper 0.43). 5 of the 6 have a significant MUA peak above 10 Hz (0.83; paper 0.62), at 10.7, 20.5, 21.5, 22.5 and 40.0 Hz; the lowest is outside 15.3 to 56.1 Hz. The coherence with amplitude averaged over long types exceeds its null (0.107) from 2.0 to 59.6 Hz without a break; averaged within each bird and then over the 3 birds, as the criterion says, it exceeds its null (0.141) over the same range. The coherence part holds; the fraction of long types, the fraction with a fast peak and the lowest peak frequency do not.
deviations: The scrambled null permutes the 1 kHz MUA samples (the reduced trace), not the raw signal, before smoothing again at 2 ms, treating the window as periodic so that no edge dip is added.

outcomes.statement: Uva activity is transiently suppressed for about 200 ms after bout offsets.
outcomes.source: Results, Song-related activity in Uva, paragraph 9; S5 Fig; Fig 4A legend
outcomes.quote: We did find, however, that Uva activity was transiently suppressed following bout offsets for a period of approximately 200ms
outcomes.notes: MUA falls below the non-singing band after bout offsets in all 3 birds but returns into it 30, 309 and 42 ms after offset (mean 127; paper about 200). It returns to the baseline level 256, 381 and 63 ms after (mean 233). Uva4 has 14 bout offsets. The suppression is present; its duration is outside the tolerance, so the outcome is partial.
deviations: Rests on the channel chosen for each bird (see fig4a-elevated-during-song).
Bout offsets are those of bouts holding song syllables; the band is the 2.5 percentile of shuffled minima over -100 to +500 ms, from random times more than 300 ms from any segment.

outcomes.statement: Uva shows little activation related to the onsets or offsets of motifs or bouts.
outcomes.source: Results, Song-related activity in Uva, paragraph 9
outcomes.quote: Finally, we find little evidence for activation in Uva related to the onsets or offsets of longer timescale song structures, such as song motifs or bouts
outcomes.notes: In Orange150 MUA before motif onsets exceeds that before other syllable onsets (0.0635 against 0.0607 V, 4.6% higher, one-sided p = 0.0012); not in b871 (p = 0.46) or Uva4 (p = 0.18). Bout onsets are not higher in any bird (p 0.78 to 0.99), and no average rises above the band after motif or bout offsets (largest excess negative in all). The claim fails on one bird's small motif-onset effect.
deviations: Rests on the channel chosen for each bird (see fig4a-elevated-during-song).
The test and level (one-sided two-sample t-test, p < 0.05) are the claims file's standard choice; the window is the 40 ms before onset of the fig6 test.

findings.statement: Each electrophysiology recording has three neural channels (5, 6 and 7, or 1, 2 and 3 for Uva4), and neither the data descriptor nor the files say which is the Uva electrode; the descriptor describes a single electrode, and its plotting script asks the user to choose 1 to 3. Only one channel per bird carries strong song-locked activity (b871 6, Orange150 7, Uva4 3), and Orange150's channels 5 and 6 are near copies of each other. The analysis files list all three channels in ChannelFiles; only Orange150's first-day file names one, running its event detectors on channel 7.
The syllable labels are not described. From the data, a to h are motif syllables, "i" introductory notes and "k" distance calls; Orange150 has no call labels.
The descriptor says introductory notes and calls are unselected (SegmentIsSelected 0), but segments labelled "i" and "k" are selected in all three birds.
The electrophysiology archive holds Bird_2-Orange150/2013-10-06.tar.gz, a second copy of the folder Bird_2-Orange150/2013-10-06 (173 files, identical MD5).
One Uva4 recording (UVA4_d000020, all four channels) has an invalid closing sample number and time, so its length and rate must be inferred from the file size.
The data set holds 3 of the 5 recorded birds, no control-lesion birds, no directed-song labels for the lesion recordings and no sorted single units, which the paper's results also rest on.

The Uva4 spreadsheet tab is named "October 6, 2016", lists recordings dated 2007-07-25 to 2007-07-27 and covers 56 of the analysis file's 178 recordings, whose times run to 2007-08-06. The Orange150 second-day tab is also named 2016. The lesion folders also hold undescribed files (SyllGaps.mat in one bird, whose durations differ from the analysis file's, and vector clustering files, two of which have the same size in two birds' folders).

verifications.by: Independent agent run by CatalystNeuro (same harness, separate context, did not write the notebook)
verifications.reviewed: Round 1. The executed notebook with the conclusion cells and the summary removed, the helper module and the claims file, with the paper's full text. The verifier checked the archive's checksums and listing and tested helper functions on synthetic inputs. The revision changed the helper and the notebook in reply (listed per claim). The revision run itself did not finish executing the revised notebook, and changed outcomes only where the round-1 numbers supported it; the revised notebook was executed afterwards (43 minutes) and is the one round 2 reviewed.

disagreements.reason: The lesion archive has only Pre-lesion and Post-lesion folders, with no directed-song label. The data description says directed song was recorded, so it may be in the folders unmarked; that makes this missing metadata more than missing data (metadata_insufficient).

Only one of 16 forms matches ("log centred", gap 300, reading a); the literal "correlation of power spectra" form rises after the lesion in 6 of 7 birds. The matching form is the author's own and not from the paper; Aronov et al. 2008 was not consulted.
The test finds a peak in 7 of 7 birds under every reading; the paper says 6, tolerance 0. In 3 birds the peak is the band edge (3.17 Hz), and thresholds of about 1.1 to 1.3 mean the test cannot fail.
EventTimes is empty and no units are sorted or identified. Raw spontaneous activity files exist (32 spreadsheet rows), but nothing says which units are HVC-projecting (metadata_insufficient).
A copy of the authors' lab's GTE extraction code from 2015 is public (kylerbrown/mindlin_auto), so this may be testable; the verifier did not check whether it compiles.
Activity falls below the band after offset in 3 of 3 birds and returns after 30, 309 and 42 ms (mean 127 ms; tolerance 180 to 220).

verifications.by: Independent agent run by CatalystNeuro (same harness, separate context, did not write the notebook)
verifications.reviewed: Round 2. The fully executed revised notebook (execution counts 1 to 40 in order), the helper module, the claims file and the attempt record, with the paper's full text. The verifier found that the record and README described the notebook as not executed, which was no longer true, and asked that the record be regenerated from the executed notebook. The round-2 revision changed the fig3 cell and added an across-bird coherence variant to fig9, sped up two helper functions without changing their results (the rhythm nulls, to keep the notebook under 60 minutes), re-ran the entry (40 minutes) and updated the record from it. No outcome changed; one change is proposed (spectral-features-weak).

disagreements.reason: The record says blocked ("not executed"), but cells 42 and 43 executed it. Under the claims file's criterion it is not_reproduced; 9 of 18 bird-feature pairs are significant in single birds under reading (a) and 15 of 18 under (b). Pooled gravity center is 0.291 (a) and 0.082 (b) against 0.17 +- 0.017, and pitch goodness and FM pass under every pooling. It should read not_reproduced, assumed, because uva.sap_features only approximates SAP (Hann taper, its own FM and pitch-goodness definitions). Cell 43 says pitch goodness, Wiener entropy and FM are significant under every reading; under the z-scored variant Wiener entropy has p = 0.06.

verifications.reviewed: Round 3. The change of outcome proposed after round 2 (spectral-features-weak) and the analysis behind it, cells 42 and 43 of the executed notebook, with the helper module, the claims file and the paper's full text. The proposal was applied; the revision re-ran the entry.

paper_notes.statement: Questions for the paper's authors. (1) Maturity index; are the spectra log-scaled and is the mean spectrum removed before correlating slices? The literal reading gives 0.32 to 0.62 and no decrease; log spectra centred per frequency give 0.235 and 0.096, as the paper reports. The Methods cite Aronov et al. 2008 for the measure; its supplement could not be read here. How is the lag correlation function normalized? (2) Which of the three neural channels is the Uva electrode in each bird? (3) How is Gamma scaled from the Lilliefors statistic, and which segmentation was used (SyllGaps.mat gives lower values than the analysis files)? (4) How were the synthetic null bouts for song rhythm built (levels, smoothing, number), and up to what frequency is R taken? (5) How was the shuffled baseline of Figs 4 and 6 built?

entries.name: danish-2017
entries.title: Uva lesions and multiunit activity in Uva during singing (Danish, Aronov and Fee 2017)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Danish, Aronov and Fee (2017) on CRCNS aa-3, which holds song from 7 zebra finches before and after bilateral Uva lesions, with the authors' segmentations, and multiunit recordings in Uva during singing from 3 of the paper's 5 recorded birds. It tests the lesion effects on song structure and rhythm, and the timing, consistency and rhythm of Uva activity relative to syllables, song amplitude and spectral song features. Control lesions, marked directed song, sorted single units and GTE times are not in the data set.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Danish et al. (2017) from CRCNS aa-3
